principle: Expectations are derived from rules stated in the repo (core/gpu.py, core/deals.py, core/stack.py, gpu-prices.json methodology) and recomputed from the live feed at run time. No price is hardcoded.

sources.repo_code: /workspace/gauge/t41/repo (core/*, mcp_server/server.py tools run in-process against the live feeds; telemetry off)

cases.intent: Can every ranked price be trusted (no unknown price, evidence attached)?
cases.expected: Every rate: price_usd and hourly_equiv_usd are numbers > 0; source_url and evidence.source_url start with https://; evidence.quote non-empty and <= 200 chars (core.gpu.MAX_QUOTE); verified_at parses as ISO-8601; the published price (price_usd, or price_per_second_usd, or server_price_usd for multi-GPU monthly) (or the whole-server hourly/monthly price for multi-GPU rows) appears as a $ amount in evidence.quote; every $ amount in 'basis' also appears in evidence.quote (basis and evidence come from the same check); marketplace offer_count / lowest_offer_usd match the counts in evidence.quote.
cases.why: Credibility rule: never show an unknown or unsourced price.

cases.intent: Monthly <-> hourly conversion uses 730 h
cases.expected: hours_per_month == 730 (core.gpu.HOURS_PER_MONTH). unit=hour rows: hourly_equiv_usd == price_usd. unit=month rows: |hourly_equiv_usd - price_usd/730| <= 0.0001 (per GPU; whole-server price = price_usd * gpu_count +-0.01).
cases.why: Agents convert monthly servers to hourly to compare; wrong basis misranks dedicated servers.

cases.intent: What is the cheapest H100 right now?
cases.expected: results sorted by hourly_usd ascending; results[0].hourly_usd == min(hourly_equiv_usd) over live feed rows whose gpu tokens include 'h100' and tier_class != reserved; scope == 'cheapest among tracked providers'; summary contains 'among tracked providers'.
cases.why: Core decision: the 'cheapest' answer must equal the feed minimum and be scoped honestly.

cases.intent: Cheapest ON-DEMAND L40S (no spot/community/marketplace)
cases.expected: Every result tier_class == 'on-demand'; results[0].hourly_usd == min over feed L40S rows with tier_class on-demand; excluded_non_on_demand == count of non-on-demand, non-reserved L40S rows.
cases.why: Agents that cannot tolerate preemption must never be handed a spot price as 'cheapest'.

cases.intent: Reservation prices are never 'cheapest'
cases.expected: Default call: no reserved rows and excluded_reserved == number of reserved H100 rows in feed. include_reserved=true: every reserved row ranks after every non-reserved row. core.gpu.estimate likewise sorts reserved last.
cases.why: 'Starting from' commitment prices need a term contract; ranking them first misleads.

cases.intent: Tier labels classify consistently
cases.expected: For every row, feed tier_class == core.deals.tier_class(row) and is in TIER_CLASSES; interruptible==true <=> tier_class=='interruptible'; any tier text containing spot/preempt/interrupt has interruptible==true; 'community' tiers -> community.
cases.why: Spot/community/on-demand filtering depends on one consistent classification.

cases.intent: Interruptible flag is backed by vendor text
cases.expected: Every interruptible==true row has vendor evidence for preemption: evidence.quote or tier contains spot/preempt/interrupt/batch-priority wording, or evidence.interruption_quote is present (non-empty, with https interruption_source_url).
cases.why: Calling a standard price 'preemptible' (or vice versa) is an invented attribute.

cases.intent: Only dedicated GPUs are compared
cases.expected: No rate where core.gpu.is_non_dedicated(gpu) is true; every rate has vram_gb as a positive number.
cases.why: Integrated/shared GPUs (e.g. Radeon 780M) are not GPU rentals.

cases.intent: Multi-GPU-only offers are represented as whole servers
cases.expected: min_gpus > 1 => gpu_count == min_gpus and server_hourly_usd (hourly) or server_price_usd (monthly) set; gpu_count > 1 => |server_hourly_usd - price_usd*gpu_count| <= 0.02 for hourly rows; tier text mentioning '8x'/'8-GPU' => min_gpus == 8.
cases.why: A 1-GPU estimate on an 8-GPU-only instance must not show 1/8 of the real bill.

cases.intent: Monthly cost for 1 GPU x 730 h is arithmetic on the feed, affiliate-neutral
cases.expected: For every hourly row: monthly_cost_usd == round(price_usd*730*billed_gpus,2) where billed_gpus = ceil(max(1,min_gpus)/gpu_count)*gpu_count; monthly rows: price_usd*billed_gpus. Order identical when every affiliate flag is flipped.
cases.why: Monthly math must be reproducible; affiliate status must never change rank.

cases.intent: 9 GPUs on an 8-GPU-only server bills 16
cases.expected: For each live 8-GPU row: monthly_cost_usd == price_usd*10*16 and calc mentions '9 requested' and '16 billed'.
cases.why: Whole-server billing (T35) on real rows, not just a synthetic fixture.

cases.intent: Is the data fresh enough to act on?
cases.expected: feed_updated_at >= max(verified_at) - 1 s and within 36 h of now; every compare result has data_age_hours <= 48 (degraded false, stale false); freshness fields next_refresh_utc / data_checked_at present.
cases.why: Stale prices presented as current are a credibility failure.

cases.intent: Held/stale vendors are never ranked
cases.expected: No (vendor,gpu) in held_stale appears in rates; held_stale entries carry a reason; compare_gpu_prices for each held GPU model returns no row from the held vendor.
cases.why: TensorDock-style stale pages must not leak into 'cheapest'.

cases.intent: What moved today? (changes feed + get_price_changes)
cases.expected: counts match change list; for up/down: pct == round((new-old)/old*100,1) (+-0.1) and sign matches direction; get_price_changes orders by core.deals rank (down, up, removed, new); next_refresh_utc at 10:23Z; non-blank data_checked_at.
cases.why: Price-move alerts drive agent re-checks; arithmetic and ordering must be right.

cases.intent: Change feed agrees with current prices
cases.expected: When changes.date == feed date: every up/down/new change's new_hourly_usd equals the current hourly_equiv_usd for the same vendor|gpu|tier|vram|gpu_count; every 'removed' key is absent from rates.
cases.why: Two public feeds must not contradict each other.

cases.intent: Site headline matches the feed
cases.expected: Homepage 'N rates from M vendors' (or equivalent) N == len(rates) and M == distinct advertisers in rates.
cases.why: Humans and agents read the site; totals must not drift from the API.

cases.intent: Unknown / near-miss model names
cases.expected: 'Z9999' -> error not_found listing tracked models; 'L40' does NOT return L40S rows (token match), i.e. not_found or only exact 'L40' rows.
cases.why: Agents must not get a different GPU than they asked for.

cases.intent: Memory size disambiguation
cases.expected: 'A100 80GB' results all vram_gb == 80; if feed A100 rows have >1 vram size, the plain 'A100' summary contains 'Memory sizes differ'.
cases.why: A100 40GB vs 80GB are different products.

cases.intent: Marketplace medians are labelled and sane
cases.expected: price_status=='marketplace' rows: tier_class 'marketplace', offer_count >= core.gpu.MIN_MARKET_OFFERS, 0 < lowest_offer_usd <= hourly_equiv_usd; non-marketplace rows have offer_count null.
cases.why: A median from 2 offers, or a 'lowest' above the median, is not a price.

cases.intent: Stack optimizer picks the cheapest pay-as-you-go GPU
cases.expected: The gpu line's monthly cost == min over core.stack._gpu_options(live feed,100,'H100') and that option is not reserved; its calc is consistent with price x 100 h x billed GPUs.
cases.why: End-to-end decision tool must agree with the comparison data.

cases.intent: GPU price-comparison page per-model summary shows the cheapest pay-as-you-go rate (reserved tier excluded, same rule as compare_gpu_prices)
cases.expected: For each model row, the lowest rate shown == min hourly_equiv_usd over that model's non-reserved rates in the live feed.
cases.why: Regression 0.3.19: CloudRift reserved rows (L40S $0.54, RTX 5090 $0.55) were shown as cheapest.

cases.intent: Every /gpu/cheapest-*-rental/ page ranks rows not marked out of stock before out-of-stock rows (same rule as /cost/ and compare_gpu_prices)
cases.expected: Within each ranked table, no row lacking 'out of stock when checked' appears after a row that has it.
cases.why: Gauge re14 K1: Oblivus H100 PCIe and Verda H100 SXM (out of stock) were mixed into the price ranking.

cases.intent: A Scout stock check older than 8 h renders unknown (stale availability) on the site and in compare_gpu_prices, and live pages expire stock claims client-side

inputs.fixture: A100 rows of gpu-prices.json with availability checked_at = now - 9 h

cases.expected: compare_gpu_prices rows have in_stock null and availability_stale true; the summary makes no in-stock claim; the site cell reads 'unknown (stale availability, last checked <ET time>)'; every stock claim on the page carries data-av-checked and the page carries the expiry script.
cases.why: Gauge re16: AVAIL_MAX_AGE_H = 8 (Scout cadence 4 h); static pages must not silently go stale between builds.

cases.intent: Served data, read without JavaScript, never carries an in-stock claim past checked_at + 8 h
cases.expected: Every in_stock:true claim has availability_expires_at and now <= availability_expires_at; no raw-HTML 'available when checked' claim is older than 8 h.
cases.why: Gauge re17 2e: static pages and feeds must not serve expired stock claims to clients that do not run JS.

cases.intent: No JSON feed or raw-HTML page lists a region past its region expiry (Scout v2.9: 1 h per region, separate from the 8 h stock claim)
cases.expected: Every available_regions_detail entry has now <= its availability_expires_at; available_regions carries regions_expires_at and now <= it; no data-rg-expires region list in raw HTML is past its time.
cases.why: Scout v2.9 (Gauge pass): region lists last 1 h; a stale region list must not be served.

cases.intent: No in-stock claim past its expiry; region-derived claims end with their regions; RunPod needs a confirmed region
cases.expected: Every in_stock=true row has now <= availability_expires_at; derived_from_regions rows have live regions_expires_at; RunPod scout rows in stock list available_regions.
cases.why: Gauge re19 N1/N2: site showed Oblivus MON1 and RunPod AP-IN-1 / H100 PCIe Secure in stock against live vendor APIs.
